summary: Cherokee National Forest fire tower site at 2,348 ft; the tower is gone, a C-15 marker remains, and a gravel road reaches the summit.

facts.status_note: The tower is gone. A marker spelling C-15 remains on the summit.

access.note: Forest Service page invites visitors to picnic there; reached by Forest Roads 311 and 198 off Highway 68, with a gravel last stretch.

visit.trail_note: Drive ends at a small parking area with steps to the grassy top. Walkers can start from a small lot on Highway 68 for a 4 mile round trip.

events.note: Tennessee lookout list marks the tower removed; Forest Service calls the site a former fire tower site. No removal date given.

notes_for_editor: Three sources agree the tower is gone: the tnlandforms list marks it removed, the Forest Service calls the site a former fire tower site, and Visit Monroe says the tower used to be there. No source gives a build date, builder, design, staffing or fire history; the story leaves those out. Conflict: Visit Monroe calls the C-15 marker stone; Mountain View Cabin Rentals calls it concrete and says pilots used it to find their position. The story attributes both and does not endorse the pilot claim, which no other page we read repeats. County: the list says Polk; the Visit Monroe page puts the trailhead a mile outside the Monroe County line, which fits Polk. A TripAdvisor search snippet says Monroe County, but that page was not fetched and is not used. Not used: AllTrails and onX snippets (Polk); a student blog on ActiveRain (unreliable elevation and unsourced claims about replacement by aerial surveillance). Searches: two WebSearch queries. Reads: tnlandforms list, Forest Service Coker Creek page, Visit Monroe page, Mountain View Cabin Rentals page, and a check of the Tennessee Division of Forestry NRHP multiple-property PDF (state towers only, no Buck Bald entry).
